question: Does my summer break count against my F-1 status if I'm registered for fall?
reference: No. A student at an academic institution is in status during the annual (summer) vacation if eligible and intending to register for the next term.

question: How many online classes can count toward my full course load each semester?
reference: No more than the equivalent of one class or three credits per term can count toward the full course of study if it is online and does not require physical attendance.

question: Can my DSO let me take fewer classes because I'm struggling with English?
reference: Yes. The DSO may authorize a reduced course load for initial difficulty with English or reading, unfamiliarity with U.S. teaching methods, or improper course placement; the student must resume a full course of study at the next available term, excluding summer.

question: I'm sick, can I drop below full time and for how long?
reference: The DSO may authorize a reduced course load, or no course load if necessary, for a temporary illness or medical condition, for up to an aggregate of 12 months at a program level, with medical documentation from a licensed professional.

question: Can I take only one class in my last semester?
reference: Yes. The DSO may authorize a reduced course load in the final term if fewer courses are needed to complete the course of study.

question: Can I be enrolled at two schools at the same time?
reference: Yes, if the combined enrollment amounts to a full course of study; the school granting the degree should issue the Form I-20.

question: I can't finish my degree before my admission period ends, can I get more time?
reference: USCIS may grant an extension of stay to a student who maintained F-1 status but cannot finish by the end of the admission period, if the DSO issues a new Form I-20 certifying eligibility.

question: What is the deadline to file an extension of stay?
reference: USCIS must receive the application on or before the authorized period of stay expires, which includes the 30-day period in paragraph (f)(5)(v).

question: I'm on OPT and want to transfer to a new school for a PhD, how soon must classes start?
reference: The student must be able to begin or resume classes within 5 months of transferring out of the school that recommended OPT or of the OPT end date, whichever is earlier.

question: What are the steps to transfer to another school?
reference: The student notifies the current school of the intent to transfer and names the new school; the current school marks the SEVIS record as transfer-out with the new school and a release date.

question: Can I work at the campus bookstore?
reference: Yes. On-campus employment includes on-location commercial firms that provide services to students on campus, such as the bookstore or cafeteria.

question: How many hours a week can I work off campus with economic hardship authorization?
reference: No more than 20 hours a week while school is in session, and only after one full academic year in F-1 status and in good academic standing.

question: My family's savings collapsed after a currency crash at home, can I work off campus?
reference: Possibly. A student may request off-campus work authorization for severe economic hardship from unforeseen circumstances beyond their control, such as substantial currency fluctuations, when other employment is unavailable or insufficient.

question: I got an offer from an international organization like the World Bank, how do I get work authorization?
reference: Apply to USCIS for employment authorization with a written certification from the international organization that the employment is within its scope.

question: Can I do OPT during my summer vacation?
reference: Yes, during the annual vacation and other times school is not in session, if the student is enrolled and eligible and intends to register for the next term.

question: How long must I be enrolled before I can do any practical training?
reference: One full academic year of full-time lawful enrollment at an SEVP-certified college, university, conservatory or seminary.

question: Do I get another 12 months of OPT if I start a master's after my bachelor's?
reference: Yes. A student becomes eligible for another 12 months of practical training on changing to a higher educational level.

question: Can students in an English language program do OPT?
reference: No. Students in English language training programs are ineligible for practical training.

question: Does the school that gave my STEM degree need to be accredited?
reference: Yes. The degree must be from a U.S. institution accredited by an agency recognized by the Department of Education at the time of application.

question: Does my STEM OPT job have to be related to my degree?
reference: Yes. The STEM training opportunity must be directly related to the qualifying degree.

question: My salary was cut during STEM OPT but my hours stayed the same, do I need to update my I-983?
reference: Yes. A pay reduction not tied to fewer hours is a material change; the student and employer must sign a modified Form I-983 and submit it to the DSO at the earliest opportunity.

question: Can my STEM OPT employer use me to replace a US worker?
reference: No. The employer attests that the STEM OPT student will not replace a full- or part-time, temporary or permanent U.S. worker.

question: Do I need an extension of stay to do post-completion OPT?
reference: Yes, unless 8 CFR 214.1(m)(1)(i) applies: the student must apply for employment authorization and either apply for an extension of stay with USCIS or seek admission through CBP after travel abroad.

question: Who has to update SEVIS before I can apply for OPT?
reference: The DSO must enter the OPT recommendation in the student's SEVIS record before the student can apply to USCIS.

question: How will I find out whether my OPT was approved?
reference: USCIS notifies the applicant of the decision in writing and, if denied, gives the reasons.

question: I'm going home for two months, can I come back and continue at my school?
reference: Yes. A student returning from a temporary absence of five months or less may be readmitted with a current, properly endorsed Form I-20 (or an updated one if there were substantive changes).

question: What do I need to re-enter the US while on post-completion OPT?
reference: An unexpired post-completion OPT EAD together with a Form I-20 endorsed for reentry by the DSO within the last six months.

question: I have off-campus work authorization and travelled abroad, can I resume my job?
reference: Only if readmitted to attend the same school that granted the off-campus employment authorization.

question: Can my F-2 spouse work in the US?
reference: No. The F-2 spouse and children of an F-1 student may not accept employment.

question: Can my wife on an F-2 visa take classes?
reference: Yes, she may enroll in less than a full course of study at an SEVP-certified school.

question: I fell out of status, can I get reinstated?
reference: USCIS may consider reinstatement requested on Form I-539 with a Form I-20 showing the DSO's recommendation, if among other conditions the student has not been out of status for more than 5 months.

question: I lost my I-20, what should I do?
reference: The DSO should issue a replacement bearing the same information, including any employment endorsements.

question: Workers at my employer went on strike, does that affect my work permission?
reference: Employment authorization is automatically suspended once the Secretary of Labor certifies a strike or labor dispute with a work stoppage in the occupation at the place of employment.

question: If my employer filed an H-1B for me, is my F-1 status extended after OPT ends?
reference: For a timely filed, nonfrivolous cap-subject H-1B change-of-status petition, status and OPT employment authorization are extended until April 1 of the fiscal year requested or the petition's start date, whichever is earlier.

question: My I-94 expired but my extension application is pending, am I still in status?
reference: Yes. A student who timely filed an extension of stay is in a period of authorized stay until USCIS decides the application.

question: How soon must the DSO update SEVIS after I go back to full-time study?
reference: The DSO must notify SEVIS within 21 days of the student's commencement of a full course of study.

question: How quickly do I need to report a new address if I'm not on OPT?
reference: Within 10 days of the change, to DHS and the DSO; notifying the DSO within 10 days satisfies the DHS notice requirement.

question: Is there a maximum number of years I can be admitted as an F-1 student?
reference: Admission is for the period needed to complete the program on the Form I-20, not to exceed 4 years, plus the additional times noted in the regulation.

question: Can I change my major during my first year as an undergraduate?
reference: No. Below the graduate level, a student may not transfer or change educational objectives within the first academic year unless SEVP authorizes an exception.

question: Can I start a second master's on F-1 after finishing my first one?
reference: Not if the first program was completed after September 15, 2026: F-1 status cannot be provided for a program at the same or a lower educational level.
